frame: Experimental Economics Replication Project (Camerer et al., 2016, Science 351:1433-1436, doi:10.1126/science.aaf0918): all 18 between-subject laboratory experimental papers published in the American Economic Review and the Quarterly Journal of Economics in 2011-2014; for each, the most important statistically significant finding as emphasized by the original authors was pre-selected and replicated with >=90% power under a publicly posted pre-registered plan. review.note: Downloaded the MPRA PDF (38 pp). Table S1 on PDF page 33 is an image, so I rendered it with pypdfium2 in the scratch venv and read it. All 18 rows were checked against frame.json, not only a sample. Table S1 order matches eerp01-18 (Abeler, Ambrus&Greiner, Bartling, Charness&Dufwenberg, Chen&Chen, de Clippel, Duffy&Puzzello, Dulleck, Ericson&Fuster, Fehr, Friedman&Oprea, Fudenberg, Huck, Ifcher&Zarghamee, Kessler&Roth, Kirchler, Kogan, Kuziemko). Replicated=No for exactly 1,5,7,9,13,14,18. These are the frame's 7 false items, so 11/18 are true, and every truth value matches. Frame completeness: the paper says 'Our sample consists of all 18 between-subject laboratory experimental papers published in the AER and QJE in 2011-2014'. experimentaleconreplications.com/studies.html lists the same 18 studies under the same p<0.05, same-direction criterion. Nothing was added or dropped, and there is exactly one item per paper (18 distinct grp values). Encoding: each txt is a faithful Persian rendering of the pre-registered hypothesis in Table S2 (PDF pp. 34-35). The txt fields contain no replication wording, no p-values and no effect sizes. The only numbers are design parameters: 80%/10%, b/c=2 vs 1.5, 60 s, eight subperiods, six-person population, three past periods. The f vectors are identical across all 18 items except eerp04 vague=true. That exception is justified by its claim text ('communication is effective'), and that item is a replicated one, so the flag does not point toward the outcome. Minor non-blocking observations: (a) the original p-values for Ambrus&Greiner (0.057) and Kuziemko (0.070) were above 0.05, but truth here is defined by the replication column, which is unambiguous for both; (b) verified_by anchor '#page=33 (manuscript p.19)' is accurate. No item's truth is uncertain, so none needs to be excluded.

frame: Reproducibility Project: Psychology (Open Science Collaboration, 2015, Science 349:aac4716, doi:10.1126/science.aac4716): replications of studies from articles published in 2008 in Psychological Science, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology and Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition; the key effect of each was fixed in a pre-registered protocol before data collection. The frame is the project's own denominator for its significance criterion: ALL 100 completed replications whose ORIGINAL result was statistically significant (97; the 3 with a non-significant original are outside the frame because the criterion 'significant in the same direction' is undefined for them — the exclusion uses only the original p-value, known before any replication). truth = replication p<0.05 with the effect in the same direction (rpp_data.csv: T_sign_R == 1 and 'Direction (R)' == same). Paper: 'Thirty-six percent of replications had statistically significant results' (= 35/97). Membership follows the project's own coding T_sign_O: studies 28, 37, 104 and 129 have a recalculated original p of 0.0503-0.0516 but the project counts them among the 97 significant originals, and so does this frame. 35/97 true. Caveat recorded for the reviewer: 113 replications were begun and 100 completed by the project deadline; the paper reports completion was not tied to outcome.
